ComBat-refQL 0.4.0 adjusts a count matrix toward a selected reference batch.
The default pathway estimates batch effects on both the mean and NB dispersion
scales while retaining biological groups and supplied covariates.

## Mean and dispersion models

After TMMwsp normalization, the mean model is

$$
\log\mu_{gj}=\log L_j+X_j\beta_g+\gamma_{g,b(j)}.
$$

For reference batch $r$, each source contrast is

$$\delta_{gb}=\gamma_{gb}-\gamma_{gr}.$$

The NB dispersion hierarchy is

$$
\log\phi_{gb}=f(A_g)+u_g+d_b,\qquad d_r=0.
$$

Thus $\phi_{gb}=\phi_{gr}\exp(d_b)$. The model contains a moderated gene
baseline and one batch-wide multiplier, without a gene-by-batch interaction.

The package first calls edgeR v4 `glmQLFit()` with shared dispersion. Working
weights from that fit determine continuous batch-specific residual information.
`estimateDisp()` supplies the moderated baseline, and a weighted NB likelihood
estimates each batch multiplier. The mean model is then refitted with the
resulting gene-by-sample NB dispersion matrix.

## QL-aware contrast moderation

The final fit supplies

$$
\widehat\delta_{gb}\mid\delta_{gb}\approx
N(\delta_{gb},s^2_{gb,\mathrm{QL}}).
$$

For each source batch, ComBat-refQL fits

$$\delta_{gb}\sim N(m_b,\tau_b^2)$$

by marginal maximum likelihood and uses

$$
\widetilde\delta_{gb}=
\frac{\tau_b^2}{\tau_b^2+s^2_{gb,\mathrm{QL}}}\widehat\delta_{gb}+
\frac{s^2_{gb,\mathrm{QL}}}{\tau_b^2+s^2_{gb,\mathrm{QL}}}m_b.
$$

Precise contrasts stay near their raw estimates; uncertain contrasts move
toward the batch prior mean. At $\tau_b^2=0$, all supported contrasts pool to
$m_b$.

NB and QL dispersions have separate roles. `fit$s2.post` scales contrast
covariance. Only the final NB dispersions enter count probabilities.

## Effective residual information

The design-only diagnostic uses

$$H^{(0)}=X(X^TX)^{-1}X^T.$$

The fitted diagnostic uses gene-level working weights:

$$H_g=W_g^{1/2}X(X^TW_gX)^{-1}X^TW_g^{1/2}.$$

For batch $b$, $\nu_{gb}=\sum_{j:b(j)=b}(1-h_{gjj})$ and the precision is

$$p_{gb}=\{\psi_1(\nu_{gb}/2)\}^{-1}.$$

Saturated strata therefore provide zero dispersion information. Weak strata
contribute continuously. A non-estimable source uses a neutral multiplier; a
zero-information reference cannot identify the full batch-scaled model.

## Counterfactual transport

For a source observation, the reference-counterfactual mean is

$$\mu^{(r)}_{gj}=\mu_{gj}\exp(-\widetilde\delta_{gb}).$$

The deterministic mid-P probability and target quantile are

$$
q=F_b(y-1;\mu_{gj},\phi_{gb})+
\tfrac12P_b(Y=y;\mu_{gj},\phi_{gb}),
$$

$$
y^*=F_r^{-1}(q;\mu^{(r)}_{gj},\phi_{gr}).
$$

The default applies this rule to zero counts. `zero_policy = "preserve"` keeps
observed zeros unchanged. Transport is deterministic and chunked. Numerical
failure rolls the complete gene back to its original counts. Reference samples
are never passed to transport and are checked for exact invariance.

## Reference selection

An explicit reference gives the clearest target. With `reference = NULL`, the
package builds a fresh locally estimable biological design inside each batch,
fits an edgeR v4 candidate model, and selects the smallest valid NB score. The
diagnostics retain every score, the selected and second-best candidates, the
margin, local design terms, omissions, and residual information.

## Method controls

The default is `ql_eb + batch_scaled`. The combinations `none + shared`,
`ql_eb + shared`, and `none + batch_scaled` provide the formal comparator and
single-component ablations. See the statistical specification and migration
guide for boundary behavior and interpretation.
